meta.title: counter.bike, an open-source bike counter for street footage
meta.description: Free, open-source software that turns street-camera footage into reviewed counts of cyclists, pedestrians, cars and motorcycles.

hero.title: Count every bike that passes.
hero.lead: Open-source software that turns street-camera footage into reviewed counts of cyclists.

showcase.alt: The review screen of the app: a list of passages, the clip of a cyclist crossing the counting line, the suggested class and a timeline of every crossing.
showcase.caption: The review screen. Every passage gets a clip, a suggested class and a place on the timeline.

route.title: Five stops from footage to count
route.lead: The software proposes. A person decides.

stops.name: Add footage
stops.title: Any fixed camera will do
stops.text: Open a file from your computer or paste a Drive link. Group the hours of one street together.
stops.alt: The library of the app with groups of street videos.

stops.name: Draw lines
stops.title: A line where people cross
stops.text: Draw counting lines at any angle and choose what each one counts: the bike lane, the sidewalk, the road.
stops.alt: The line editor with counting lines drawn over a frame of the street.

stops.name: Detect
stops.title: Everything that moves is a candidate
stops.text: Object detection and motion tracking find each passage. A vision model suggests its class, blurred night riders included.
stops.alt: Frames of one passage, cut around a cyclist, as the vision model receives them.

stops.name: Review
stops.title: Accept, correct or add by hand
stops.text: Enter accepts a suggestion and a number key changes it. Missed someone? Shift and a number counts them while the video plays.
stops.alt: The original video in the review screen, with the counting lines on top and the bar for counting by hand.

stops.name: Export
stops.title: A video and a spreadsheet
stops.text: Get the footage with a running counter burned in, a CSV of every passage and a JSON report.
stops.alt: A frame of the final video with the counter panel over the street.

checked.title: Checked against counts made by hand
checked.lead: Detection is the first pass. The review closes the gap.
checked.caption: Two streets, one evening each, compared with counts made by hand

rows.where: Augusto de Lima bike lane, 5 to 8 pm

checked.note: What the detector missed is added by hand. What it doubled is discarded.

statement.title: Cities build for what they count.
statement.text: counter.bike is working toward one open count of cyclists, worldwide. It starts with your street.

contribute.title: Four ways to help
contribute.lead: The code, the models and the method are public.

rows.title: Improve the models
rows.text: Blurred bikes at dusk still get missed.

rows.title: Publish footage
rows.text: Labelled clips teach the detector your city.

rows.title: Translate
rows.text: The app speaks eight languages. Add the ninth.

rows.title: Count by hand
rows.text: Counts added by hand become ground truth.

close.title: It runs on your own computer

facts.text: NVIDIA is faster. A processor alone works.
Your own OpenRouter key, about 18 US cents per thousand passages

close.alt: A frame of the final video: the street with the counter panel showing totals per category.
close.caption: A frame of the final video, with the counter burned in.

download.title: Download counter.bike
download.lead: Free for Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.firstRun: On its first run the app installs its detection engine, so keep the internet on.

credits.title: Licence and credits
credits.lead: counter.bike is free software, built on other people’s free software.
credits.licenceText: Distributed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Use it, study it, change it and share it. If you distribute a changed version, or offer it to others over a network, publish its source under the same licence.

The design system behind this site
credits.weights: The detection weights, including the model tuned for blurred bicycles, derive from Ultralytics YOLO and carry the same AGPL-3.0.

donate.title: Keep the count open
donate.lead: counter.bike is free and stays free. Donations pay for what volunteers cannot give.
donate.soon: Donation channels are being set up. Until they open, the best gift is a labelled clip from your street.
